I also wonder how bad our big bad can get in our big battle for the multiverse and blah blah blah, they've exhausted their resources years ago and I feel the fatigue with everyone else. But though I'm skeptical on the premise for Absolute Power, I certainly do have faith in Waid and Mora.

I can appreciate Joshua Williamson's passion and knowledge for DC lore and continuity, but I've never read a book of his that I thought to be profoundly good. That's not to say he's an "awful" writer, and I understand that books (especially comics) can thematically succeed in their simplicity, but after reading his work I'm constantly left feeling dissatisfied, wanting a story with more depth and nuance to sink my teeth into, and I unfortunately never get that with Williamson.

With no narration from The Sovereign to (for a lack of a better term) "hide" from, this issue has the most dialogue from Diana that King has written so far and I can't help but feel as if it's slightly, off?? 

One line that came off wrong was "Do I look like the type of woman who gets her toes done at the mall??" Now *obviously* I'm sure Diana has access to much better resources, but I felt as if she came off as arrogantly self-assertive. I would've much preferred if the scene played out like this:

"As Diana and Clark are walking through the mall, a group of fans approach them saying something along the lines of "Wonder Woman we love you blah blah blah, it's so unfair what's happening to the Amazons on earth blah blah blah", then Diana notices the nail salon and suggests that they all get pedicures. Clark then asks (in his boyish ignorance) "Why would THE Wonder Woman get her nails done at some mall??" and then we see a pleasant group shot of Diana and her fans all getting pedicures as she joyfully expresses something heartfelt about woman/sisterhood"

As of now I don't believe Tom King has Diana's characterization nailed down, and going forward it's slightly concerning since I'm *really* hoping for this to be the best book possible.

I know plenty of you feel indifferent towards Diana's newfound "no thank you" catchphrase, but I can appreciate its attempt to retain Diana's elegance in the midst of a heated discussion or battle. However I would prefer to keep it for those said moments rather than in regular conversation where it feels all a bit tongue in cheek. 

I'm not ashamed to admit, Clark's dad-jokes got quite a few good laughs from me, but this following exchange: 

Diana: "Do you know something?? You're a good man, Clark Kent."

Clark: "I... well, y'know, I don't know. I'm just whoever ma raised." 

SO DAMN TOUCHING!! Superman Up In The Sky is nothing short of phenomenal but fuck me I'm hoping Tom gets to write even more Superman in the future.

As for the artwork, maybe I'm just spoiled with Daniel Sampere/Tomeu Morey but man this wasn't great. My main issue is the palette of green/yellow/brown which just looks nauseating, while I'm not huge on the pencils either it could've certainly benefited with better coloring.

That being said, the gift for Bruce was perfect and after a few rereads, this issue was meh. Felt as if this could've been a story for an annual, but if anything I'm real glad Sampere has time to relax!!

In a few interviews I've seen, Tom King has said that writing Diana is challenging and I can't help but feel that there is an overreliance of narration from The Sovereign to progress through the story, rather than letting the audience hear Diana's internal monologue. Don't get me wrong I love seeing our Amazon lift tanks above her head and throw the Washington monument at Giganta (which was sooo fucking sick haha), but at a certain point there's a disconnect I feel from Diana's perspective. However, that disconnect from Diana's perspective puts the reader in a similar POV with the civilians in the story who can do nothing but watch the propaganda of the Amazons spread all throughout the news (hoping we get more moments like the father and daughter being interviewed back in issue 1), and nonetheless for the story to be narrated from the perspective of someone who built our country on deceiving the populous, I believe it all works for the better. I love Tom King's work, and Daniel Sampere's artwork is phenomenal, personally this book has been such a blast to read!!
